aspect: Nobody knows how big it is
description: The GAO concluded the extent of elder abuse by guardians nationally is unknown, citing missing data on how many guardians serve older adults, how many adults are under guardianship, and how many cases of abuse occur.
energy_note: Unmeasured, by the body whose job is measuring it.

aspect: EXAMPLE - what the sampled cases contained
description: GAO identified hundreds of allegations of physical abuse, neglect and financial exploitation by guardians across 45 states between 1990 and 2010; in 20 closed cases, guardians stole or improperly obtained $5.4 million from 158 incapacitated victims.
money_note: Mean per victim across the 20 closed cases.
energy_note: Five point four million, from a hundred and fifty-eight people.

aspect: Three quarters of it is financial
description: Case analysis found three-fourths concerned financial mismanagement or breach of fiduciary duty - unfiled accounts, improper expenditure, selling property without authority, changing a beneficiary to themselves.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the oversight that did not happen
description: Courts ignored guardians' criminal and financial problems and failed to review irregular accountings. In one case a $31,000 federal tax lien was filed against a guardian a month after her appointment and she was allowed to continue; in another a social worker served simultaneously as guardian, conservator, representative payee, therapist, landlord and service provider to one victim.
energy_note: Six roles, one man, one old woman's money.

description: A prosecutor observed that most financial exploitation by professional guardians occurs through overcharging for services either unnecessary or never performed - lawful-looking invoices rather than theft.
